what: Nike is the largest seller of athletic footwear and clothing in the world. It designs and markets shoes and apparel under the Nike, Jordan and Converse brands and has them made by contract factories in Asia, selling through its own stores and app and through retailers.
customers: Consumers worldwide, sold both directly and through wholesale partners such as sports retailers and department stores.
money: running, basketball, training and lifestyle shoes
moat: The most valuable brand in sport, built on decades of athlete endorsement, plus scale in design and sourcing no rival matches.
risks: Revenue has shrunk about 3% a year over three years as lifestyle sneaker demand cooled
Operating margin fell to about 8%, far below its historical level
Cutting back wholesale partners to push direct sales lost shelf space to competitors
Newer running brands have taken share in its core category
opportunities: A new chief executive has refocused the company on sport and on rebuilding retail partnerships
Inventory clean-up is largely finished, which should let margins recover
Return on invested capital of about 12% even in a weak year
watch: Revenue growth in North America and whether gross margin recovers.
